# Methods of Presentation of Aeronautical Information

D.E. Eshmuradov$^{1}$, T.D. Elmuradov $^{1}$, N.M. Turaeva$^{2}$

$^{1}$  Tashkent State Technical University named after Islam Karimov, Tashkent, Republic of Uzbekistan

$^{2}$  Tashkent University of Information Technologies named after Muhammad Al-Khorezmi, Tashkent, Republic of Uzbekistan

Abstract: Progress in the development of computer technology makes it possible to solve an increasingly wide class of tasks using software systems, among such tasks is the task of automatic processing of aeronautical information. This makes it necessary to use new approaches to the design and development of such systems. One of these approaches is based on the application of the idea of collective activity of a set of agents - multi-agent technologies. In this regard, the purpose of the article is to consider the features of the implementation of automated processing of aeronautical information based on multi-agent technologies. To achieve this goal, a problem-structural methodology for the synthesis of hybrid systems was chosen, which allows creating self-organizing models, each element of which develops, receiving data and knowledge from other elements. In the course of the study, a formal definition of a multi-agent system for automatic processing of aeronautical information is presented, which includes many agents; the environment of agents' functioning; a set of permissible relationships between agents; a description of the rules for forming a network of agents; a set of individual and joint actions, communication interactions, behavioral strategies and actions; the possibility of system evolution. Also, detailed attention is paid to the description of each agent, for which the author suggests using four elements: a set of variables, inputs and outputs, an autonomous method that performs appropriate changes on a set of variables. It is proposed to use the following as agents: notification agent for pilots, agent of preflight newsletters, agent of data creation, agent of aviation processes, agent of aviation database formation, agent of aeronautical maps creation, agent of export/import of aeronautical data set, agent of publications and reference books. In addition, the article presents a schematic representation of a multi-agent system for automated processing of aeronautical information and describes in mathematical terms in detail the process of processing an application in an agent. The results obtained in the course of the study can be used to increase the effectiveness of the analytical component in the structure of the system for the formation of direct and reverse coordination links in the process of solving air navigation problems.

Keywords: automation, processing, multi-agent system, air navigation, process, environment, airspace.

## INTRODUCTION

Increasing the degree of technical equipment with modern means plays an important [12173]

role in expanding the possibilities of using airspace. The rapid development of information technology has given impetus to the improvement of air navigation systems in both civil and military aviation. Measures are planned to introduce automated air traffic control systems (ATC) complexes using modern equipment, software, system construction technology, as well as a human-machine interface that takes into account the recommendations of the European Organization for the Safety of Air Navigation [1]. The aeronautical information received by the equipment of users of satellite radio navigation systems makes it possible to solve the tasks of controlling aircraft and various military facilities at a qualitatively new level, i.e. information about the structure of the airspace in paper or electronic form. The structure of the airspace of the territory is information about airfields (air hubs) concerning the characteristics and actual condition of airfields, about the order of air traffic in the area of airfields, about air routes and their equipment with radio equipment, as well as other information necessary for the organization, execution and management of flights [2].

Modern high-precision navigation systems are based on the use of inertial navigation systems, which can be supplemented by both satellite correction systems and navigation systems for the geophysical fields of the Earth. For example, the automatic on-board flight control system (ABSU) of the Tu-154M aircraft includes 75 components that can operate in 7 different modes, in addition, they interact with 12 on-board systems and are a complex dynamic analog complex [3]. On international airlines, to drive aircraft in automatic mode, they can be equipped with the KLN-90 GPS navigation satellite system or use the UNS flight control system. Given this complexity, the amount of load on the crew and flight safety in general largely depends on how reliably the ABSU works.

In such conditions, there is a need to integrate the aeronautical components of various systems, which will ensure the functioning of automated control systems, improve mobile response to changes in the situation, and achieve functional stability of the flight navigation complex of the aircraft in certain flight modes. There is no doubt that this task can be solved through the use of tools and complexes for automatic processing of aeronautical information.

Moreover, a number of requirements are put forward for the automatic processing of aeronautical information, namely:

\- digitization of aeronautical data, which will allow users to manage critical information for flight safety and optimize processes;

\- отображение display based on the digital information used with a time and geographical representation of the actual situation, for example, closed runways and taxiways, temporary routes, etc.;

\- Full support of the verification and validation process in accordance with the RTCA DO-2008 regulation to meet the requirements for data quality in terms of accuracy, resolution, integrity, traceability, etc.;

\- guarantees that aviation data will be tracked throughout the chain of their receipt to identify errors;

\- an automated process of verifying the integrity of a data element, in which a certain element is compared with information from another source, either from another process, or from another point in the same process[4].

## RESEARCH METHODS AND METHODOLOGY

To solve this problem, it seems appropriate to use a problem-structural methodology for the synthesis of hybrid systems. The choice of this methodology is due to the fact that it provides a fundamental opportunity to solve complex practical tasks that constantly arise in the process of processing aeronautical information without simplification. It also allows you to create self-organizing models, each element of which develops, receiving data and knowledge from other elements. In addition, within the framework of this approach, it is possible to develop models of systems relevant to the original, which is confirmed by successful examples in various subject areas. The value of this methodology specifically for aviation navigation and the huge data flow produced by various systems that ensure its functioning lies in the fact that it allows you to create and experiment with a large number of methods that adapt to continuous changes in the composition and structure of heterogeneous tasks, directs the evolution of ways to accumulate, process and present information, according to the vector designated by the system developer.

## RESEARCH RESULTS

A multi-agent system is grouped agents of an information network that interact with each other and achieve the goal set by the developer [5]. In order to ensure the interconnection of all three levels of decision-making within the automatic processing of aeronautical information: operational, strategic, goal-setting, it is necessary for a multi-agent system to form a single information picture - an information image that can be represented in the form of an "information user - process - environment" configuration.

To solve the problems of proactive management, a multi-agent aeronautical information processing system should combine such latest technological achievements as data mining, mobile technologies, modeling technologies, decision support and implementation of management impacts in real time, as well as integrate tools for both support and purely decision-making [6].

The formal definition of a multi-agent system for automatic processing of aeronautical information has the following form:

$$
\text {AgentNet (Agnt, Env, Rel, Org, Act, Com, Evol)}
$$

where, Agnt - multiple agents;

Env - agent operating environment;

Rel - the totality of permissible relationships between agents;

Org - description of the rules for forming a network of agents;

Act - a set of individual and joint actions, behavioral strategies and actions;

Com - a set of individual and joint actions or communication interactions;

Evol - the possibility of system evolution.

Each agent $Agnt_{i}, i = \overline{1, n}$ can be described using four elements:

$$
A g n t _ {i} = \langle S t a t e _ {i}, X _ {i}, Y _ {i}, P r o c e s s _ {i} \rangle
$$

where $State_{i}$ - a set of variables that completely define $Agnt_{i}$,

$X_{i}, Y_{i}$  - inputs and outputs $Agnt_{i}$ , subsets $State_{i}$ , the elements of which are associated withEnv;

$Process_{i}$ - an autonomous method that performs the appropriate changes over $State_{i}$.

The following elements can act as agents of the system:

1. Notification agent for pilots, implemented through the NOTAM module, which connects the automatic functions of international and national NOTAM departments, such as the creation, storage, distribution and search of NOTAM, in full compliance with ICAO standards. It covers NOTAM, ASHTAM, AIM, AIM and CRAM and helps to harmonize NOTAM formats.

2. Agent of preflight newsletters. This agent can be implemented through the PIB Bulletin Portal solution, which creates standard bulletins and summaries based on data from FIRs (Flight Information Region), airfields, routes, polygons, restricted airspace, levels, time and all parameters known from the NOTAM Q line. This allows you to get minimized PIB (Pre Flight Information Bulletins) with four-dimensional content directly related to the flight. It eliminates irrelevant NOTAMs and can take advantage of the update service and scheduler functionality.

3. Data creation agent. The purpose of this agent is to maintain a continuous electronic chain of ICAO data for obtaining and publishing the necessary aeronautical information. It provides a platform for the integration of all information, functions, processes and stakeholders of the aeronautical data chain across organizational boundaries through a web interface, taking into account the functions of the ICAO for the collection, comparison and provision of accumulated information.

4. Aviation Process Agent - necessary to support procedures for obtaining, approving and publishing aeronautical data. The functioning of this agent will ensure that the raw data received is evaluated, approved and stored in a predetermined sequence, and all actions are registered legally.

5. An agent for the formation of an aviation database, its purpose is to collect all the necessary information for PBN (Performance based navigation), terrain data, obstacle data, airfield mapping data (AMDB), NOTAM management, as well as aeronautical maps.

6. Aeronautical Chart Creation Agent - The development of aeronautical charts and charts covers the entire life cycle of publishing maps from map definition and automatic creation to detecting changes, updating and creating output data.

7. Aeronautical Data Set Export/import Agent - thanks to this agent, a continuous chain of formation, use and transmission of electronic aeronautical data is provided, which have a structured form and allow the next intended user to use and verify the received data.

8. Agent of publications and reference books. This agent provides integrated quality process control for the publication of AIP, AIP Amendment, AIP Supplement, AIC and other flight and airfield management manuals. The agent is necessary so that the changes made are as simple, understandable and fast as possible for publication.

AmongEnvcan be served through the elements:

$$
e n v = \langle S t a t e _ {e n v}, P r o c e s s _ {e n v} \rangle
$$

An important feature of this representation of the environment is that it is active in itself, contains its own $Process_{env}$, which can change $State_{env}$ regardless of the agents included in this environment. The structural elements of the Env environment can be represented by corporate databases and data warehouses, a knowledge base and a database of models, various transactional and analytical systems, mail servers, document management systems, and the like.

For effective interaction between the levels of a multi-agent system for automated processing of aeronautical information, presented in the form of an information user – process–environment configuration, it seems appropriate to use the concept of multi-level intelligent systems. The multilevel approach implements an interaction model in which a set of components of an intelligent system interact and exchange knowledge in some internal representation [7]. The block diagram of the model is shown in Fig. 2.

The assignment of various groups of agents that make up the scheme of a multi-agent system for automated processing of aeronautical information, presented in Fig. 2, allows them to be combined into various functional subsystems. For example, subsystem [S1] is responsible for the formation and analysis of the image of automatic processing of aeronautical information. In the environment of this subsystem, data collection agents interact with each other, which are programs that collect and consolidate information to solve mission control tasks.

The navigation map creation agent is a modeling agent that interacts in the environment of the solution modeling subsystem [S2] and demonstrates high efficiency in its intellectual implementation. This agent learns from experience and can offer the most suitable model of calculations and analysis, including hybrid.

The agents from block [S3] are the agents of searching for rules and precedents, which act as components of the subsystem of searching for solutions in the knowledge base. They can be reactive, create an ensemble of agents in the process of solving the tasks put forward for them. For the most part, reactive structures are characteristic both for agents of influence functioning in the environment of the subsystem of formation and implementation of managerial influences [S4], and for agents of presentations from the interface subsystem [S5].

Agents of studying user preferences should be cognitive, only in this implementation they can perform the tasks assigned to them [8]. Accumulation and processing of knowledge of such agents is carried out on the basis of the knowledge base [KB], for example, using ontologies.

Let's take a closer look at the application processing process in the agent.

With the appearance of the request R at the agent's input, in the case when it can be processed, the promotion of data packets begins in the agent. The packet C at time  $\tau$  is a four, which consists of the unique identifier of the current request u☐N, the alphabet of the data processed by M, the current data d for processing, the agent and the path P that this packet passed (an ordered subset of the elements of the latter):

$$
C ^ {\tau} = \langle u, M ^ {\tau}, d ^ {\tau}, P ^ {\tau} \rangle , P ^ {\tau} \subseteq A
$$

By $\tau = 0$ have $M^{\tau} = X', d^{\tau} = x, P^{\tau} = \{\}$. After processing the package by the element $a_{t}(t \in [1, n])$ for example, parts M and d change according to the original alphabet of the current element and the results of the conversion:

$$
\boxed { \begin{array}{l} \left\{ \begin{array}{c} M ^ {\tau + 1} = Y ^ {t} \\ d ^ {\tau + 1} = f _ {a _ {t}} (d ^ {\tau}) \\ P ^ {\tau + 1} = P ^ {\tau} \cup a _ {t} \end{array} \right. \end{array} }
$$

Next, the packet  $C^{(\tau+1)}$  is transmitted to the following elements. The agent is assigned the task of determining which of the elements needs to transfer the specified package. The latter can only be delivered to the element that has the corresponding input alphabet [9]. Therefore, when deciding on the destination of the package, the agent forms a selection of elements from the set of available ones (those that can process the current data), guided by the results of the analysis of the current state of the system. Such a sample size of m elements can be described as follows:

$$
\left\{a _ {i} \middle | M ^ {\tau} \subseteq X ^ {i} \right\} \subseteq A, i = \overline {{1 , m}}
$$

It should be noted that a situation with multiple routes is possible when an agent has elements in its composition whose input alphabets intersect:

$$
m > 1 \Rightarrow \exists j, k \in [ 1, n ]: X ^ {j} \cap X ^ {k} \neq \{\}
$$

Changes in the operation of the system can be implemented by modifying package delivery solutions through the agent's graph G. The agent must choose the route with the lowest cost to promote the package. Then, when such a route is unknown, the packet is broadcast to elements that can process the data transmitted internally. Of all the possible routes formed in this way, choose those that give the minimum time to pass the packet. Such routes are remembered and used for further processing of relevant applications [10].

Based on its current state and set of functions $\varphi$, the agent can decide on the "undesirability" of passing a packet along a certain arc of the graph $G$ or the route. In this case, the agent can slow down the passage of data along the selected arc and thus adjust the route selection.

Thus, the agent gets the opportunity to change the ways of processing incoming requests depending on its own goals, which are determined by the cost function $\varphi$ . Such a reconfiguration of the route is carried out if an element appears in the agent's structure that may be part of an alternative route, or is able to change the cost of application processing routes [11].

## CONCLUSION

The multi-level agent model proposed in the article makes it possible to implement automatic processing of aeronautical information in the configuration "information user - process - environment" and is based on the integration of modern information technologies for data accumulation and analysis. The agent-oriented approach of intelligent data processing used in its construction makes it possible to ensure parallel execution of operations at the levels of users of aeronautical information, the process of its accumulation, collection and analysis, the circulation environment, and also makes it possible to distribute the development of necessary solutions among specialized agents, manage knowledge, organize transitions between proactive management processes and ensure the integration of various information systems, methods, modes of data preparation and analysis within one model.
